Approved evidence

HCAST

benchmark.metr-hcast

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

The full HCAST primary paper and pinned public README/LICENSE support a source-defined benchmark family with human-calibrated tasks, scoring and quality controls. Original Time Horizon inputs, internal code/scoring groups and the public example subset are scoped components of this family, not new families. A separate bounded identity review corroborates the source-defined benchmark boundary. Pinned README deprecation remains historical; no full withheld-payload, current maintenance, reproduction or upstream rights clearance is asserted. Actual author, separate source-verifier and adversarial source-content review records bind every approved claim at its exact scientific digest. This metadata classification does not freeze core eligibility.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HCAST · adjudicated: HCAST baseliners commit work to a repository and record screens and spoken work through Loom; the authors manually review most successful baselines, prioritizing unusual times and disagreement among attempts.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.hcast.baseline-recording-and-correction.v1

  • Some early baselines were collected without screen recording.
  • Authors review all reported score or clock errors and report implementing score changes in 30% of reported cases and time changes in 71% of reported cases; these percentages concern reports, not all baseline attempts.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HCAST · recruited: HCAST recruited technical human baseliners mainly through METR employees’ professional networks and required the large majority to pass domain-specific qualification tasks before main-suite work.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.hcast.baseliner-recruitment-and-qualification.v1

  • Typical backgrounds were a degree from a top-100 global university or more than three years of relevant professional experience; this is a description of the recruited pool, not a universal expertise guarantee.
  • General-reasoning tasks have no separate qualification: passing a qualification in any domain suffices, while the two specified cryptography tasks additionally require demonstrated cryptography expertise.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HCAST · benchmark task: Each HCAST task supplies instructions, a container where the agent runs as the agent user, and a scoring function running as root; continuously scored tasks are binarized at heuristically chosen success thresholds.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.hcast.container-and-score.v1

  • Most tasks already return binary scores, and scoring code is hidden from agents by default with task-specific exceptions.
  • Human baseliners use the same task environment and instructions, but receive some additional web access and the exact success thresholds even when agents are not told those thresholds.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HCAST · documents: HCAST’s author-assigned contamination categories include 125 tasks with private solutions, 31 with public solutions judged hard to memorize, and 33 with public solutions judged easy to memorize.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.hcast.contamination-strata.v1

  • The private-solution subtotal comprises 86 tasks with private problem statements and 39 with public problem statements.
  • These labels are author judgments and may be mistaken, including when a similar problem exists elsewhere without the authors’ knowledge.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HCAST · benchmark task: HCAST v1 contains 189 individually created tasks: METR employees and contractors created 143, while 46 came through its independent-contributor task bounty.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.hcast.human-task-construction.v1

  • The paper groups these tasks into 78 internal task families sharing setup code and scoring logic; those internal groups are components of this benchmark.
  • The authors target software engineering, machine learning, cybersecurity and general reasoning activities that can be completed by writing and running code, with limited reliance on vision or other modalities.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HCAST · filtered: HCAST combines fresh-human task testing with manually reviewed agent attempts: an unexposed person attempts a task in most task families, and reviewers read all 945 transcripts from five agent attempts on each of the 189 tasks.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.hcast.manual-task-quality-control.v1

  • Agent QA usually used Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new), with other models sometimes used; reviewers checked both unintended successful exploits and failures caused by missing resources or scoring errors.
  • Gold reference solutions were implemented where feasible for regression checks when tasks were revised.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HCAST · documents: The HCAST v1 human reference comprises 563 attempts by 140 people, including 341 successful attempts; 110 tasks use the geometric mean of successful baseline times, and 79 use forecasts by a task creator or familiar author.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.hcast.measured-and-forecast-human-times.v1

  • Of the 79 tasks without a successful baseline, 29 had only unsuccessful human attempts and 50 had no collected baseline; forecasts therefore are not measured successful completion times.
  • The authors report remaining timing errors as a limitation, despite retroactive correction of egregious timing-software errors.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HCAST · human annotation: HCAST reports paying baseliners $50–100 per hour plus $25–150 per hour in performance bonuses; Appendix E.2.1 defines a successful-completion bonus of (r/2)×t, where r is the baseliner’s hourly rate and t is the average time spent on that task by all baseliners.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.hcast.paid-human-incentives.v1

  • A further r×t bonus rewards the fastest successful completion; if no attempt succeeds, that speed bonus is shared equally among those who attempted and failed.
  • A small number of early baselines used hourly wages without these incentives, and the authors describe the speed incentive as pushing estimated human times toward a lower bound.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HCAST · access terms: The HCAST v1 paper releases 11 example task families and withholds the remainder to limit contamination and hill-climbing; the captured hcast-public README identifies its contents as a subset and marks the tasks deprecated.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.hcast.public-subset-license-and-access.v1

  • At commit 03438239d200fb3e89a5ddfc62ab4d23cc1866fb, the public repository is MIT licensed, with copyright and permission-notice retention required; the repository separately makes informal requests against training-data inclusion and exposed solutions.
  • The README says some task assets are stored in DVC and must be downloaded to inspect them; the public repository’s terms and subset description do not establish access to the full withheld benchmark.
